status: RATIFIED STRUCTURE (D-132) — item wording remains draft until practitioner review and pilot. NOT a published question bank.
supersedes: teacher-v1.6.0-clinical-review-draft.json (and the 2026-08-06 compression pass, replaced by the hybrid change set)
governing: D-089 (as amended by D-119 and D-132)
D-132 (Teacher Intake v1.6.1 ratification — universal baseline capture, conditional depth)
ratificationLanguage: Teacher Intake v1.6.1 adopts universal domain consideration through concise baseline observation capture. Additional clinical detail is conditional on identified concerns, developmental applicability, and evaluation planning relevance. Future revisions should be guided by practitioner review and observed completion data rather than predetermined expansion of the instrument.

pattern.baseline: Affirmative baseline checklist, capped at five statements per domain, shown whatever the disposition (except 'Not enough opportunity to observe'). Derived from the district referral form's per-domain fields — not freely authored.
pattern.yes: Baseline + deficit-phrased difficulty checklist + topography/extras (Behavioral only) + ONE optional example field + Step-3 depth
pattern.no: Baseline only. No free-text field on this path.
pattern.not_observed: Baseline is skipped as well. Observation gap stored explicitly; never rendered as 'No'.
pattern.baselineHint: Check what you have observed this student do. Leaving an item unchecked means you have not observed it or it does not apply at this grade — it is not recorded as a difficulty.
pattern.difficultyHint: Check the difficulties you have observed. Leaving an item unchecked means it is not a difficulty you have observed — it is not recorded as a strength.
pattern.uncheckedRule: 'Not observed' is carried by the disposition, never by an empty checkbox. One meaning per list.
pattern.capRule: Initial baseline item cap: five items per domain, subject to clinical bank review and pilot validation (D-132). An authoring bound, not a burden-governance ceiling — burden remains governed by pilot-measured completion, abandonment, and clinical yield (D-119). Enforced in question-bank.schema.ts.

steps.title: About your work with the student

emergencyNotice.text: Do not use this form to report an emergency or an immediate threat to the student or another person. Follow your school or district's urgent-response procedures now.
emergencyNotice.open: District-approved escalation message and workflow still to be supplied — see openQuestions.

step1.note: Displayed from the case record. The teacher never re-enters grade; grade-band routing depends on data that exists before the invitation is sent.

step1.prompt: Which subjects or settings do you share with this student?
step1.note: Converted from short text — same information, no typing, machine-readable, and lets the form check a domain disposition against whether the respondent actually sees that setting.

step1.prompt: How long have you worked with this student?
How often do you work with this student?
step1.note: Duration and frequency license the 'not enough opportunity to observe' reading downstream.

step1.prompt: What are this student's strengths and interests?
step1.note: This required item is why no referral can produce a deficit-only picture, independent of what any domain checklist does.

step1.prompt: Have you noticed a marked change in, or loss of, skills, behavior, or mood this student previously demonstrated?
followup: What was the student previously able to do?
Approximately when did you notice the change?
step1.note: A 'Yes' here is one of the highest-signal answers on the form and always opens the three follow-ups.

step1.prompt: Are attendance or tardiness affecting this student's access to instruction?
followup: Briefly describe the pattern you have noticed, and how it affects the student's progress.
step1.note: First-class Step-1 item (relocated from Other/Miscellaneous). Attendance qualifies every other domain's data — it belongs with the observation window.

step1.prompt: Are you aware of health, medical, or environmental factors that may be affecting this student at school?
followup: Briefly describe what you have observed at school.
step1.note: Relocated from Other/Miscellaneous, kept light and school-observable (nurse visits, medication administered during the day, absences for appointments). A teacher is not the source for medical history — that is parent intake and records.

step1.prompt: Have you observed any of the following? (Vision and hearing access screen)
options: Appears to have difficulty seeing instructional materials
Squints, moves unusually close, or loses place visually
Frequently asks for spoken information to be repeated
Turns one ear toward speakers or appears not to hear consistently
step1.note: Replaces the Step-2 Vision & Hearing domain. Vision and hearing are an access variable and an exclusionary consideration — no strengths profile, no severity gradient, no evaluation-planning depth. Screening records are assembled at case level; teachers are never asked records questions. 'None observed' never implies screenings passed or are on file.

domains.note: Attention/organization items (BEH.B1, BEH.B3, BEH.D1–D3, BEH.D7, BEH.D9) are authored once here and mapped to their constructs. The teacher answers once; the evidence may inform Behavioral, Cognitive, and ADHD/OHI consideration through construct mapping. No duplicate item set exists anywhere in the bank (D-132).

domains.note: Teacher input here is attributed classroom observation of learning and thinking. It is never an informal ability estimate and is never scored or summed. Attention evidence arrives via the Behavioral construct mapping — attention is not re-asked here.

domains.note: The baseline list is newly authored for v1.6.1 — the prior draft's always-shown items were deficit-phrased, which broke the one-meaning-per-list rule. Capped at four; no fifth item is forced to exist to reach the cap.

items.prompt: Have you observed behavior at school that has placed, or could reasonably place, the student or another person at risk of harm?
items.followup: Briefly describe what happened and approximately when.

items.prompt: Has the student said or done anything that has caused you concern about self-harm, suicide, or the student's immediate safety?
items.followup: Briefly describe what you saw or heard, and approximately when.

safety.notice: If you have an immediate safety concern, do not wait for this form. Follow your school or district's urgent response procedure now.
safety.rule: Always asked regardless of disposition, with the escalation sentence rendered beside each item. Yes sets the case priority flag server-side, independent of form submission or summary review. The two items deliberately overlap on self-harm: one measures observed behavioral risk, the other a statement indicating ideation — a student can present either without the other.
safety.escalationWording: OPEN — the district-approved escalation message and workflow following a Yes are still to be supplied. The items ship; the message cannot ship without it.

autismObservationSet.name: Autism-related observation questions
autismObservationSet.namingRule: Never presented or referred to as a screener (D-132). Rename only if replaced by a validated screening instrument.

trigger.prompt: Have you observed persistent repetitive behavior, strong inflexibility around changes or routines, or unusually focused interests that affect the student's participation at school?
trigger.shownWhen: Communication, Social/Emotional, or Sensory is marked Yes
trigger.note: Asks only what was observed — no 'may warrant closer review' clause. Teachers report observations; routing is the system's job.

autismObservationSet.setOpensWhen: Trigger is Yes, OR Communication, Social/Emotional, and Sensory are all marked Yes
items: Uses repetitive movements, speech, play, or object use
Shows marked distress with change, transitions, or unexpected events
Has unusually intense or narrow interests that affect participation
Repetitive routines or rituals interfere with classroom participation
autismObservationSet.scaleRationale: Frequency drives the actual decision — whether autism-specific instruments enter the battery. A four-point verbal frequency with no neutral midpoint keeps that information without presenting as a scorable rating scale.
autismObservationSet.reductionRationale: The social-communication half of the picture (back-and-forth interaction, eye gaze and gesture, peer relationships) is already collected under Communication and Social/Emotional; the prior set's sensory item restated the entire Sensory domain. Only the restricted/repetitive half is collected here, once.
autismObservationSet.optionalExample: Describe one example that would help the psychologist understand the observed pattern.
constraints: Never presented as an autism probability
Never determines diagnosis, eligibility, or test selection

step3Blocks.title: Academic performance and intervention
step3Blocks.when: Shown when Reading, Math, or Writing is marked as a concern.
checklists: Supports or accommodations currently in place
Graphic organizer, models, or worked examples
step3Blocks.note: Untouched — the only place objective evidence enters from the teacher, and the only structured answer to the response-to-intervention question.

step3Blocks.title: Context and what has been tried
step3Blocks.when: Shown when Adaptive Behavior, Social/Emotional, Behavioral, Cognitive, or Motor Skills is marked as a concern. Asked once across those domains, not repeated per domain.
prose: Where or when is the concern most evident?
Impact is asked once, in Step 4 — the near-verbatim duplicate is removed (v1.6.1).
What has been tried, and what happened when it was used?
One combined response — splitting 'tried' from 'what happened' produced two half-answers.

step3Blocks.title: Communication follow-up
step3Blocks.when: Shown when Communication is marked as a concern.
checklists: With complex language or multi-step directions
Affects being understood, understanding others, or participating

step3Blocks.title: Sensory follow-up
step3Blocks.when: Shown when Sensory is marked as a concern. Frequency and impact rather than peer comparison.
fields: How often do these responses interfere with participation?
prose: What helps the student settle or participate?

step4.prompt: Overall, how do the concerns affect the student's learning, participation, relationships, independence, or access to instruction?
step4.condition: Required when any domain is marked Yes; not shown otherwise.
step4.note: Sole home of the impact question — the Step-3 duplicate is removed.

step4.prompt: Which of these are available if the evaluation team needs them?
What is the most important area where you would like this student to make progress?
step4.condition: Optional; shown when a concern is reported.
step4.note: The one-year question, kept as a short prompt — it reframes the referral from cataloguing what is wrong to describing what meaningful progress looks like, feeding intervention design, IEP planning, and parent communication.

step4.prompt: Is there anything else the evaluation team should understand?
step4.note: Always shown. This is what makes cutting Other/Miscellaneous safe — the residual has somewhere to go, without a disposition attached to it.

outputLicensing.licenses: “No concerns were reported in this area at this time.” Nothing further.
A short affirmative paragraph built only from what was selected, followed by that same conclusion. Populates the district referral form's per-domain strengths field.

An attributed concern paragraph using only the specifics given — never escalated in severity, frequency, or cause — alongside the affirmative baseline selections for the same domain. A concern-flagged domain still produces a strengths picture; that is the point of the universal baseline.
“Not enough opportunity to observe was reported by this informant.” Never rendered as no concern, and never used to check the district's N box.

changesFromV160: Baseline affirmative capture restored in every domain, capped at five statements, shown whatever the disposition — conditional depth, not conditional existence (D-132). Grounds: the district referral form carries a per-domain strengths field and RIE populates the district's document — an output contract, not narrative enrichment.

One meaning per list: baseline lists are affirmative in every domain, difficulty lists deficit-phrased in every domain, each under its own ratified hint string. Sensory's baseline newly authored (its prior always-shown items were deficit-phrased).
Free text reduced to one optional example field per domain, on the Yes branch only. The No-branch optional data-point field is removed.

Vision & Hearing removed as a Step-2 domain; its four observable signs become the Step-1 access screen (S1-10). The two 'has available screening information' records questions are deliberately not carried over.
Other/Miscellaneous removed as a domain; attendance and regression are first-class Step-1 items, health/medical/environmental context is a light Step-1 item (S1-09), the residual is caught by Step 4.

Autism set renamed 'Autism-related observation questions'; reduced from seven items to the four restricted/repetitive items; five-point Likert replaced by four-point verbal frequency (Never observed · Occasionally observed · Frequently observed · Not sure).
Step-3 functional block no longer asks impact — Step 4 is the impact question's sole home, required when any concern and not shown otherwise.
Step-4 'Which current supports are most helpful?' cut — supports are already collected in structured, actionable form (accommodations checklist + intervention response rating).
One-year question shortened to one optional prompt, shown when a concern is reported.
Available-data checklist expanded to the nine-option list including 'None known to me'.
Subjects/settings converted from short text to multi-select.
Per-domain magnitude comparison scales dropped from this draft; magnitude remains an open decision (if reintroduced: non-academic domains only).

openQuestions.detail: The universal baseline partly solves attention visibility — Behavioral's baseline always shows, so attention observations always exist. The remaining depth case: a teacher who flags Cognitive but not Behavioral sees no attention difficulty items. Fix by surfacing the same authored item set from either entry point, one construct mapping, with a simple entry-provenance tag. Do not author a second set; do not build an elaborate provenance system (D-132).

Which baseline and difficulty items require early-elementary, elementary, middle, secondary, or ungraded applicability. Phonological awareness is the clearest case. Unblocked, since grade comes from the case record before the invitation is sent.

D-132 derives baseline item sets from the district referral form's per-domain fields. That field-by-field mapping needs to be produced and attached, or the cap has no anchor and the lists drift back to freely authored.

Absent from this draft. If reintroduced, non-academic domains only — for Reading, Math, and Writing the academic block already collects a score, and a teacher severity judgment beside a benchmark number is the weaker of two fields that can then contradict each other.
The district-approved message and workflow following a Yes on either safety item. The items are restored before this is settled; the message cannot ship without it.

openQuestions.topic: Taxonomy gap — speech fluency and voice (carried from v1.6.0)
openQuestions.detail: The district asks about stuttering (repetitions, prolongations, blocks) and voice quality (nasal, hoarse, breathy). The taxonomy has LANG.ARTIC but no construct for either. Those two items are tagged to the parent LANG and flagged — they need a taxonomy v0.5 addition before this becomes a bank, or their evidence will be under-specified.
